modern: From Alexander the Platonist, not to say to anyone, often or without need, or to write in a letter, that I have no time; nor continually to excuse the neglect of the duties required by our relationship with those we live with, by pleading urgent business.
original: From Alexander the Platonic, not frequently nor without necessity to say to any one, or to write in a letter, that I have no leisure; nor continually to excuse the neglect of duties required by our relation to those with whom we live, by alleging urgent occupations.

notification_original: From Alexander the Platonic, not frequently nor without necessity to say to any one, or to write in a letter, that I have no leisure…

explained.summary:
Alexander the Platonist taught Marcus not to keep saying, or writing, that he had no time, and not to dodge his duties to the people around him by pleading that he was busy.

’I’m too busy’ can become a habit and an excuse. The obligations we owe to family, friends and colleagues don’t go away because something else feels urgent.
explained.today: Think of the reply that starts ’Sorry, mad week’, sent for the third month running, or cancelling on a friend again because work got busy. Busyness is real, but it can quietly become the reason you never show up.
